title: Books reimagined: AI to create new experiences for things you know — Lukasz Gandecki, TheBrain.pro
talk_summary: A demo-driven talk about an AI-enhanced book reader that adds scene-aware music, character avatars, embedding search, and voice Q&A, built by rapid vibe-coding then gradual hardening. The transferable content is mostly about iteration style and refactoring economics, not agent orchestration.

takeaways.technique: Waves of AI rewrite then harden
takeaways.what_they_do: Iterate with fast AI-generated rewrites early, and only once change amplitude drops switch to tests and refactoring.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the amplitude of the waves is getting lower and lower and there comes the time where I can start old school engineering

takeaways.technique: Refactor priority = badness x pain x ease
takeaways.what_they_do: Decide refactors by multiplying how bad, how painful, and how easy the code is, skipping bad-but-untouched code.
takeaways.evidence_quote: how bad the code is multiplied by how painful I multiply by how easy

takeaways.what_they_do: AI produces the initial draft and humans do the taste/quality pass where AI cannot judge.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the AI does the initial draft and we do the rest

takeaways.what_they_do: Have the LLM emit structured XML metadata (scene, characters, mood) that downstream code consumes deterministically.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we also do structured XML with metadata

takeaways.technique: Embedding search plus scoped deep research
takeaways.what_they_do: Use embeddings for natural-language recall and a bounded deep-research pass that reads only up to the current point.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's going to actually read the whole book till the to the point that you finished at
